info.title: Marro API
info.description:
Server-to-server access to one organization’s data in Marro. Each key belongs to an organization and can use only the scopes it was given for modules the organization subscribes to. Keys go only in the Authorization header, over HTTPS, from a server: never in browser code or a URL. A key that was ever sent over plain HTTP or in a URL must be treated as leaked: revoke it and create a new one. The API sends no CORS headers.

Every response carries `X-Request-Id`, to quote to support. Once the key is checked, responses also carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets) for whichever limit is closer to running out. An address that is not an endpoint answers 404 `NOT_FOUND` in the same error shape.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Record-link custom fields accept numeric target ID arrays (one or up to 20 according to recordLink.multiple). Reads resolve accessible targets to id/kind/name/href objects. Deleted, archived, disabled and inaccessible targets are omitted. Destinations require the corresponding leads.read or crm.records.read scope; user destinations have no public API scope. Object destinations use object:<id>, require objects.records.read and the key creator current object grants.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Contacts, companies and enabled opportunities with record-type custom fields. Dedicated crm.records scopes are required.

tags.name: Reference
tags.description: How this organization is set up: fields, stages, sources and people.

tags.name: Money
tags.description: Products, quotes, invoices and payments. Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit (paise, cents); a new document is in the organization's own currency. Tax follows the organization's regional settings: under India GST an invoice carries CGST and SGST inside the organization's state, IGST outside it, and no GST without a supplier GSTIN; under a single-rate tax (Australia GST 10%, UK VAT) each taxed line carries that tax (singleTaxMinor), and none without the supplier's registration number. Each document keeps the tax it was issued under (tax.model).

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Custom reports shared with everyone in the organization, and their figures. Built in the app under Reports → Custom reports; a key reads them over every lead.

The key needs its own custom-object scope and its creator must still be an active user with the matching object grant. Own/team/all scope is checked on every read and write. post.description:
Creates a lead with the organization’s own field rules: required fields, option lists and formats are checked exactly as in the app. The lead starts in the starting stage unless you give one, and without an owner the organization’s assignment rules pick one. Phone number and email are unique per organization, so a retry of the same lead returns DUPLICATE_LEAD with the existing ID instead of creating a second.

Scope: `leads.write`.

fields.description: Values by field key. `name` and `phone` are always required, plus any field the organization requires on create. `source` takes a source ID and `assigned_to` a user ID; without an owner the organization’s assignment rules decide.

stageId.description: Defaults to the starting stage of the lead’s pipeline. A stage names its own pipeline.

pipelineId.description: Defaults to the organization’s default pipeline. With a stageId, the stage must be one of this pipeline’s.

branchId.description: The lead’s branch (IDs from GET /api/v1/branches). Without one the lead takes its owner’s branch, if they belong to one.

401.description: UNAUTHORIZED: The key is missing, wrong, revoked or expired.

403.description: FORBIDDEN: The key lacks the scope, or the organization’s plan does not include it.

409.description: DUPLICATE_LEAD: A lead with this phone number or email already exists; `details.leadId` is its ID when known.

422.description: VALIDATION_FAILED: A field is missing or invalid; `details.fields` says which. A refused stage, pipeline, owner, source or branch gives `details.reason` (for example `STAGE_NOT_IN_PIPELINE` or `BRANCH_NOT_FOUND`) and `details.field`.

post.description:
For website and landing-page forms. Adds the enquiry as a new lead, or, when the organization already has a lead with this phone number or email (matched ignoring case), fills in that lead instead: only fields it has empty are filled, and values that differ from what your team entered are kept and listed on the lead’s timeline. The owner, stage and pipeline of an existing lead are never changed, and an archived lead is not changed at all (the enquiry is noted on its timeline). A new lead starts in the starting stage and gets an owner from the organization’s assignment rules. Every capture is recorded on the lead’s timeline, naming the API key that sent it.

Server to server only: call it from your website’s server (a route handler, a server action, PHP), never from browser JavaScript, where the key would be visible to anyone. There is no CORS support on purpose.

Retries are safe: send an `Idempotency-Key` header (or an `externalId`), and a repeat within 24 hours returns the first result without capturing again.

Scope: `leads.capture` or `leads.write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A unique value per submission, such as a UUID; remembered per API key. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first result, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is refused.

phone.description: With the country code, e.g. +919812345678. Numbers without one are read as Indian. Used, with email, to find a lead the organization already has.

email.description: Also used to find an existing lead when the phone number does not match one.

source.description: The source’s name, e.g. "Website" (the default) or "Google Ads". It must be one of the organization’s active sources (matched ignoring case; list them with GET /api/v1/lead-sources). Any other name is recorded as "Website", so a website key cannot fill the organization’s source list.

pipelineId.description: For a new lead, the pipeline it starts in (IDs from GET /api/v1/pipelines); it lands in that pipeline’s starting stage. Defaults to the organization’s default pipeline. Never moves an existing lead.

notes.description: Free text shown on the lead’s timeline with this enquiry, such as the visitor’s message.

fields.description: More details, by field key: the organization’s built-in and custom lead fields (GET /api/v1/lead-fields). Values are checked with the same rules as the CRM’s forms: dropdowns take one of their options (value or label), numbers, dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and yes/no fields are parsed. An unknown key is refused with the list of valid keys. On an existing lead only empty fields are filled.

x-codeSamples.source:
<?php
// In wp-config.php (never in a theme file anyone can read, never in JavaScript):
// define('CRM_API_KEY', 'mk_live_...');

$response = wp_remote_post('https://app.marro.si/api/v1/leads/capture', [
    'timeout' => 10,
    'headers' => [
        'Authorization'   => 'Bearer ' . CRM_API_KEY,
        'Content-Type'    => 'application/json',
        // One ID per submission; reuse it if you retry and the CRM captures it once.
        'Idempotency-Key' => wp_generate_uuid4(),
    ],
    'body' => wp_json_encode([
        'name'   => sanitize_text_field($_POST['name'] ?? ''),
        'phone'  => sanitize_text_field($_POST['phone'] ?? ''),
        'email'  => sanitize_email($_POST['email'] ?? ''),
        'source' => 'Website',
        'fields' => [
            'city' => sanitize_text_field($_POST['city'] ?? ''),
            'interest' => sanitize_text_field($_POST['interest'] ?? ''),
        ],
        'attribution' => [
            'pageUrl'  => esc_url_raw(wp_get_referer() ?: ''),
            'formName' => 'Contact form',
        ],
    ]),
]);

if (is_wp_error($response) || wp_remote_retrieve_response_code($response) >= 300) {
    // Keep the enquiry (for example, email it to yourself) so no lead is lost.
    error_log('CRM capture failed: ' . (is_wp_error($response) ? $response->get_error_message() : wp_remote_retrieve_body($response)));
}

x-private-native-objects.unknownOutcome: Retain original requestId and complete canonical input. Read-only exact-input reconciliation; no automatic network retry/new key. not_found never executes the request.
x-private-native-objects.privacy: Bounded public-key DTOs; no internal value slots, private history, full answers or receipt contents. Titles/counts exclude inaccessible records. No-store and Vary Authorization.

ApiKey.description: An organization API key, created in Settings → Integrations → API keys. Keys start with `mk_live_`. Marro stores only a hash of a key, so it is shown once, when it is created: copy it then. Revoking a key ends its access at once. To replace a key without downtime, create the new one, switch your server to it, then revoke the old one. Changes made with a key appear on the lead’s timeline as made by the person who created the key, via the API. Scopes: `objects.records.read` (Read custom objects), `objects.records.write` (Create and update custom-object records), `objects.records.delete` (Delete custom-object records), `leads.read` (Read leads), `leads.write` (Create and update leads), `leads.capture` (Capture leads), `crm.records.read` (Read customers and opportunities), `crm.records.write` (Create and update customers and opportunities), `reports.read` (Read reports), `money.read` (Read products, quotes, invoices and payments), `money.write` (Create quotes and invoices and record payments), `agent.tools` (AI agent tools (MCP)).
